subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A shape-memory alloy such as Nitinol is useful because it:
options: Glows in the dark after exposure to light
Returns to a pre-set shape when heated
questions.explain: Shape-memory alloys can be deformed and then return to their original 'remembered' shape when heated above a transition temperature.

An alloy of copper and zinc
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy made by combining copper and zinc, giving it good corrosion resistance and machinability.

questions.q: Which is an example of a new or emerging technology used in modern manufacturing?
questions.explain: Additive manufacturing such as 3D printing is a newer technology transforming how prototypes and products are made.

questions.q: When selecting a material for a children's outdoor playground slide, the most important property is:
options: Durability and weather resistance with a smooth, non-toxic finish
questions.explain: An outdoor slide must withstand weather and repeated use safely, so durability, weather resistance and a smooth non-toxic surface are the priority.

questions.q: A product life cycle assessment considers the impact of a product:
options: From raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal
Only while it is being used
Only at the point of sale
questions.explain: A life cycle assessment evaluates environmental impact across the whole life: extraction, processing, manufacture, distribution, use and disposal.

questions.q: A non-ferrous metal is best described as one that:
options: Is harder than any ferrous metal
Is always an alloy of two metals
Contains no iron and does not rust
questions.explain: Non-ferrous metals such as aluminium and copper contain no iron, so they are generally not magnetic and do not rust.

questions.q: Malleability is the property that allows a material to be:
options: Hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking
Returned to its original shape after a force is removed
questions.explain: Malleability is the ability of a material to be deformed by compression, such as hammering or rolling into sheets, without breaking.

questions.q: Planned obsolescence refers to designing products that:
options: Are deliberately made to have a limited useful life so they are replaced sooner
Last as long as technically possible
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence is the practice of designing products with a limited lifespan to encourage repeat purchases.

questions.q: Which is a natural fibre rather than a synthetic one?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural fibre grown from the cotton plant, whereas polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic fibres made from polymers.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the 6 Rs of sustainability?
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are reduce, reuse, recycle, refuse, rethink and repair; 'rethink' encourages designing in more sustainable ways.

questions.q: Corrugated cardboard is widely used for packaging mainly because it is:
options: Extremely heavy and rigid like steel
Lightweight, low-cost and provides good impact protection
questions.explain: The fluted middle layer of corrugated card gives strength and cushioning while keeping the board light and cheap, ideal for protective packaging.

questions.q: 'Repair' as one of the 6 Rs is more sustainable than replacing because it:
options: Sends the product to landfill sooner
Extends a product's life and saves the resources of making a new one
Always costs more than a new product
questions.explain: Repairing a product keeps it in use for longer, saving the energy and raw materials needed to manufacture a replacement.
